questions.question: What factors contribute to the rise of climate refugees?
questions.solution_html:
• Around 90 million of the current 123 million forcibly displaced people are living in
  • countries with high-to-extreme exposure to climate-related hazards. Climate refugees
  • are not refugees as per the UN convention of refugees - Climate change increases the
  • risks of extreme weather events – like storms, floods, wildfires, heatwaves and droughts
  • – making them more unpredictable, frequent and intense. At the same time, rising sea
  • levels, droughts and drastic changes in rainfall patterns as a result of warmer
  • temperatures can destroy crops and kill livestock, threatening livelihoods and
  • exacerbating food insecurity.

questions.question: When was the UNFCCC established? Examine its role in mitigating the climate / crisis.
questions.solution_html:
• UNFCCC was established in 1992-coordinate global efforts against climate change
  • provides a platform for negotiation-including the Kyoto Protocol and Paris Agreement
  • facilitates climate finance and adaptation support- promotes emission monitoring
  • encourages cooperation to limit global temperature rise and strengthen climate resilience.
questions.final_answer: encourages cooperation to limit global temperature rise and strengthen climate resilience

questions.question: What are some common ozone-depleting substances? Explain.
questions.solution_html:
• Common ozone-depleting substances- include chlorofluorocarbons, halons- carbon
  • tetrachloride-methyl chloroform-these chemicals release chlorine and bromine in the
  • stratosphere- breaking down ozone molecules- reduction under the Montreal Protocol has
  • helped restore the ozone layer and prevent harmful ultraviolet radiation impacts.
questions.final_answer: helped restore the ozone layer and prevent harmful ultraviolet radiation impacts
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain how wetland drainage affects their role as methane sinks or sources.
questions.solution_html:
• Wetland drainage exposes organic-rich soils to oxygen- increasing microbial
  • decomposition and releasing methane- converting wetlands from methane sinks to sources
  • reduces water saturation- alters vegetation, disrupts carbon storage- accelerates greenhouse
  • gas emissions-undermining wetlands’ natural climate-regulating functions.
questions.final_answer: gas emissions-undermining wetlands’ natural climate-regulating functions
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Discuss the role of the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) in / shaping India's climate policy

  • solar energy- energy efficiency-sustainable agriculture- water conservation- integrates climate
  • goals with development-promotes low-carbon planning- encourages renewable energy
  • expansion- frames long-term mitigation and adaptation strategies across sectors.
questions.final_answer: expansion- frames long-term mitigation and adaptation strategies across sectors

questions.question: Discuss the historical context that led to the establishment of the Ministry of / Environment and Forests (MoEF) in India.

questions.question: Analyze how the Kunming-Montreal Framework contributes to climate change / mitigation.
questions.solution_html:

  • that store carbon- restoring degraded landscapes-reducing deforestation- promoting

questions.question: Discuss how invasive species are affected by climate change and the implications / for native biodiversity
questions.solution_html:
• Climate change accelerates the spread of invasive species -by altering temperature-rainfall
  • habitat conditions that favour their expansion-invasives outcompete native species- disrupt
  • ecosystems-reduce biodiversity- intensify ecological stress-posing new challenges for
  • conservation and ecosystem management.

questions.question: What are the primary drivers of biodiversity loss, and how do they impact / ecosystems and human well-being?
questions.solution_html:
• Primary drivers of biodiversity loss- include habitat destruction- climate change-pollution
  • overexploitation- invasive species- these pressures disrupt food webs- degrade ecosystem
  • functions- reduce species populations- undermine services like pollination- water
  • purification- climate regulation-ultimately threatening human health, livelihoods, long-term
  • ecological stability.

questions.question: What is the greenhouse effect, and how do global initiatives like the Paris / Agreement aim to mitigate its impact on climate change?
questions.solution_html:
• Greenhouse effect is the natural process where gases like CO₂ trap heat in the atmosphere
  • warming the Earth-human activities intensify this effect- leading to climate change- Paris
  • Agreement aims to reduce global emissions- limit temperature rise to well below 2°C
  • strengthen adaptation- enhance climate finance- promote global cooperation to mitigate its
  • impacts.

questions.question: What are the core objectives of India’s National Action Plan on Climate Change / (NAPCC), and how effective has it been?

  • energy efficiency- water conservation- sustainable agriculture- seeks low-carbon growth and

questions.question: When was the UNFCCC established? Examine its role in mitigating the climate / crisis.

  • facilitates climate finance and adaptation support- promotes emission monitoring
  • encourages cooperation to limit global temperature rise and strengthen climate resilience.

  • tetrachloride-methyl chloroform-these chemicals release chlorine and bromine in the

questions.question: Explain how wetland drainage affects their role as methane sinks or sources.
questions.solution_html:
• Wetland drainage exposes organic-rich soils to oxygen- increasing microbial
  • decomposition and releasing methane- converting wetlands from methane sinks to sources
  • reduces water saturation- alters vegetation, disrupts carbon storage- accelerates greenhouse
  • gas emissions-undermining wetlands’ natural climate-regulating functions.
questions.final_answer: gas emissions-undermining wetlands’ natural climate-regulating functions
